elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.1A expressly permits the Customer to terminate “this Agreement or its participation in this Agreement for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.1A permits termination upon thirty days’ prior written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The other Parties must refund pro rata all Customer-prepaid amounts attributable to the period after termination becomes effective.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Other Parties may terminate unilaterally only at the end of the 25-year Initial Period or thereafter; during that committed period, termination otherwise requires unanimous written agreement.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The Customer may terminate on thirty days’ notice, rather than being subject to a 60-to-90-day notice period.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee applies to the Customer’s Subparagraph 18.1A termination, so the conditional cap is satisfied. The no-credit provision applies only to termination under Subparagraph 18.1.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.1 permits any Party to terminate at the end of the Initial Period “or any time thereafter,” not solely at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Any Party exercising the Subparagraph 18.1 termination right must provide at least one year’s prior written notice, which exceeds 90 days.
